conviction_note: Three small positive read-throughs (Elevance's same-day Medicaid and ACA commentary, and no MOH 8-K or pre-release since 22 July, unlike July 2025) sum to +2.1. The scaled number is only +0.48 (abs 12 x p_up 52) because this name has risen after 1 of its last 8 prints, ELV itself reportedly fell on its beat, the stock is +14% over 20 days into the print, and the Q3 call is where Molina has historically given its first look at the next year (Oct 2025: -17.5%). The gap between +2.1 and +0.48 is that reaction history, not a disagreement about the facts.
bar: Company FY2026 guide: adjusted EPS at least $5.25 (raised $0.25 on 2026-07-22), GAAP at least $2.15, premium revenue ~$42bn, with Q4 carrying a $1.50/share Florida Medicaid start-up loss (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001179929/000117992926000036/moh2q26_er.htm). Q3 consensus EPS of ~$0.72-0.73 comes from the sweep row's wire read only (Earnings Whispers), not two agreeing estimate sources, so the quarterly bar is effectively single-sourced and every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest ~2.9M shares, ~5.6% of float, ~1.4 days to cover, Equibles snapshot ~2026-08-20 (https://equibles.com/stocks/moh/short-interest), via the sweep row; I could not refresh it (Nasdaq short-interest API returned 503). This is not a crowded short. 25-delta skew is -1.41 vol points (calls marginally bid over puts, so 'balanced'), and the put/call open-interest ratio is 0.33, which is call-heavy. Event-implied move is 10.7% on a 57% ATM IV. Run-up is +3.2% over 5 days and +14.0% over 20, and the stock is 11% below its 52-week high.

findings.finding: Elevance's Q3 2026 release and call (2026-10-21, 8:30 a.m. ET, before this window opened) said Medicaid is 'tracking slightly ahead of our prior full-year margin guidance', that July 1 rate updates 'did provide greater support to the second half margins', and that Medicaid cost trend is 'elevated, but relatively stable compared with the second quarter'. Its consolidated benefit expense ratio was 90.6% against 91.3% a year earlier. Molina is ~90% Medicaid by membership (4.42M of 4.93M at 2026-06-30) and its Q2 Medicaid MCR of 92.7% was 'in line with expectation'. So the largest Medicaid peer reporting after Molina last spoke supports a Q3 Medicaid MCR at or better than plan, against a ~$0.72 Q3 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-22 Medicaid came in line and Medicare came in better than expected, guidance was raised $0.25, and the stock fell 9.67%, so the Marketplace miss dominated. On 2026-04-22 the stock rose 14.18%. Seven of the last eight prints fell, so this name has not paid for in-line Medicaid. Investing.com reports ELV itself fell ~2.2% today after its $6.99 vs ~$4.70 beat, because ~$1.85 was non-operating.
findings.why_not_priced: ELV printed this morning and MOH's sealed spot of $215.95 at noon ET already holds part of it. MOH's +3.2% over 5 days and +14% over 20 suggest the market had been leaning toward a Medicaid trough before ELV spoke. If the read-through were fully priced, MOH's skew would be call-bid and its implied move compressed. Instead the skew is near flat and the event-implied move (10.7%) sits close to the historical median (12.1%), so the market still prices a two-sided print.
findings.independence: UnitedHealth's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-13) lowered its MCR to 88.4% from 89.9% and raised guidance, but it gives no Medicaid-specific cost commentary, and it included $610M of favorable reserve development (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000731766/000073176626000255/earningsrelease3q26unh.htm). This is a different document and points the same way, weakly. ELV's own 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001156039/000115603926000068/a3q2026elvearningsrelease.htm) is the same event as the transcript and is counted once here. It is a proxy: Molina has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: Elevance said Individual ACA performed ahead of expectations, with a modestly higher full-year ACA operating margin, and that 'we feel pretty good about where the 2027 rates have landed'. Its 8-K credits Individual ACA as a driver of the 70 bp lower benefit expense ratio. Marketplace was Molina's problem line in July: a $1.50/share guidance cut on higher-than-expected cost trend, with a Q2 Marketplace MCR of 88.9% that was 'higher than expected'. A peer's ACA book running better argues against a second Marketplace cut at this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Marketplace cut on 2026-07-22 (offset by Medicare +$1.50) came with a -9.67% reaction despite a net raise. Marketplace surprises have been the line this stock has traded on recently.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out this morning, and the sealed noon spot partly holds it. The read-through is weak: Molina's Marketplace is ~283k members, and its problem was its own cost trend, which ELV's bronze-mix risk-adjustment comment does not map onto directly. If the market had fully priced an ACA all-clear, put skew would sit well below calls, and at -1.41 it barely does.
findings.independence: Same event as finding 1 (the ELV release and call), but a different line (ACA, not Medicaid). Net of the rest of the company: Marketplace is a small share of premium, so even a clean Marketplace quarter moves the guide modestly unless Medicaid confirms. No independent second source.

findings.finding: EDGAR shows no Molina 8-K since the 2026-07-22 Q2 release (only the 10-Q, 13G filings, and routine quarter-start director Form 4s on 2026-07-02 and 2026-10-02). In 2025 Molina pre-announced a guidance cut by 8-K on 2025-07-07 (bmo, -2.91%) before its print. The absence of a pre-release this cycle, with the FY guide 'at least $5.25' outstanding, makes a large unflagged guidance cut somewhat less likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-07-07 pre-release moved -2.91%, and the 2025-07-23 print after it moved -16.84%. A pre-release did not stop the full print reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an absence, and any market participant could have observed it. It is mostly priced, which is why it is sized small. It would be fully priced if the implied move had compressed below the historical median, and it has not (10.7% against 12.1%).
findings.independence: None. This is an inference from the filing record, sized near zero under the rule that an absence is weak evidence.

findings.finding: Molina's FY2026 guide already carries a $1.50/share Q4 loss from the new Florida Medicaid contract and a $1.00/share loss from the traditional MAPD product it exits for 2027. The CEO called 2026 'the trough year for Medicaid pretax margins' and said the building blocks 'position us well for profitable growth in 2027'. Any 2027 commentary on this call lands against that framing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At the Q3 2025 print (2025-10-22), the first look at the next year came with a -17.49% move. The 2026-02-05 initial guide came with -25.51%. The forward-year line has produced this name's largest moves, mostly down.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 Florida and MAPD items sit inside the company's guide, so they are priced, and the finding is sized at 0. It is filed because it sets the 2027 bar the call will be judged on. I found no sourced 2027 consensus, so its direction cannot be sized.
findings.independence: ELV said states should 'incorporate more of that cost trend' into 2027 rates and expects Medicaid margins to improve in 2027 (https://gloom.sh/stocks/elv/transcripts/q3-2026). That leans the same way as Molina's 'trough' language but does not size Molina's 2027.

outside_window.finding: Centene announced on 2026-10-19 that it will host its Q3 2026 call. The date was not visible to me, but Centene typically reports after Molina, so its Medicaid and Marketplace read lands after this window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Molina 8-Ks or press releases since 2026-07-22: none on EDGAR (the IR press-release page returned 403)
Centene Q3 2026 results: not yet released as of the IR page on 2026-10-21
UnitedHealth Q3 2026 Medicaid-specific cost or rate commentary: none in the release

rejected_candidates.candidate: Elevance's 2025 'Medicaid trough' commentary and cost-trend warnings from October 2025 coverage
rejected_candidates.detail: Dated to the Q3 2025 print, a year old. Superseded by the 2026-10-21 Q3 2026 release and call used in finding 1.

rejected_candidates.candidate: UnitedHealth's Q3 2026 consolidated MCR improvement and guidance raise as a separate Medicaid finding
rejected_candidates.detail: No Medicaid breakout, and the improvement is driven by reserve releases and commercial/MA, so it is filed as weak independence under finding 1 rather than as a finding of its own.

baseline_tension: The positive peer read-through agrees with the +14% 20-day run-up and the call-heavy open interest. That makes it partly priced, and it cuts against this name's history of 7 of 8 prints falling, so p_up is held at 52 rather than the ~57 the peer evidence alone would suggest.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; 7 of 8 prints fell, and ELV was sold on its own beat): Medicaid read-through cut from +1.5 to +1.2, and p_up from 53 to 52.
Rule 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest): ACA read-through cut from +0.8 to +0.6, because Marketplace is a small share of premium.
Rule 5 (an absence is weak evidence): the no-pre-release finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 6 (a bar inside the guide, and a single-sourced quarterly bar): added the Florida/MAPD guide item at 0, kept every size capped small, and cut print_vs_bar from 5 to 4.
